| rf_ask_plain | The address of the agency's data service for programs, and any file kept beside it that lists the requests it accepts. |
| rf_fail | No OpenAPI or Swagger document was found at the data-interface addresses recorded for this agency; where no address is recorded at all, the fail says only that none was found in the sources searched. It is not a claim that the agency has no data interface, that its interface is undocumented, that it publishes no machine-readable description anywhere (a description at a developer page, or in another format such as a catalog document at the interface's root, is not looked for), or that its interface refuses programs. |
| rf_fix_line | Publish a machine-readable description of the data interface where the interface is served. |
| rf_hypothesis | Does the agency publish a machine-readable description of its data API? An SI client that is to call an API rather than scrape pages needs to know the calls, their parameters and what they return; a description a program can read lets it build the call without a person reading documentation first. |
| rf_name_brief | A published description of the agency's data service |
| rf_not_measured | The public client could not look at one or more recorded addresses, for one of three reasons: the host refused the identified client; the client's own compliance with the site's robots.txt kept it from the recorded address; or it could not confirm an absence because a recorded address was left unverified or a seed source unsearched, or a server or network error occurred. |
| rf_partial | Some of the recorded addresses served such a description and some did not. |
| rf_pass | A machine-readable OpenAPI or Swagger description document is served at the data-interface address recorded for this agency, and the result names that address. Every address that was looked at met this. |
| rf_plain_name | OpenAPI description served at the recorded API address |
| rf_question | Does the agency publish a machine-readable description of its data interface, so that a program can learn the available calls and build one without a person first reading the documentation? |
| rf_requirements | [{"source": "w3c-dwbp-2017", "quote": "Provide complete information on the Web about your API."}, {"source": "w3c-dwbp-2017", "quote": "It will also enables machines to access the API documentation in order to help developers build API client software."}, {"source": "openapi-specification-core", "quote": "allows both humans and computers to discover and understand the capabilities of a service"}, {"source": "rfc-9727-api-catalog", "quote": "they SHOULD make that metadata available at the API endpoint URIs they have listed"}, {"source": "w3c-dwbp-2017", "quote": "Check that every call enabled by your API is described in your documentation. | rf_rung_two_changes | The description document is usually public and needs no key; but this check reads the recorded data-interface address, which could itself require a key, so registering as a member of the public and presenting one could let the client reach a document a bare request cannot. |

| rf_what_client_does | The public client makes one web request to the recorded address and reads whether what comes back is a machine-readable description, meaning a document carrying the OpenAPI or the Swagger marker, at one request per second and never a path the site's robots.txt disallows. |
| rf_where_we_look | At the data-interface address recorded for the agency in the project's records (read from the agency's own pages or seeded from a named source such as a developer page or a public catalog), and any description document recorded beside that address. |
| rf_who_else | Google Lighthouse runs this kind of check: anyone can run its automated checks against a named page, its criteria are published, and a result comes back met, not met, or not applicable. It does not run this exact one. |
| rf_why_it_matters | A W3C practice says to provide complete information on the web about an interface so that machines can read it, and USAFacts' AI-ready data guide calls for data interfaces; requiring the description to be OpenAPI and to sit at the recorded address is the project's own rule, and the project has marked this check not yet valid. |
| rf_why_short | A World Wide Web Consortium practice asks for service details that programs can read; the required file format is this project's rule. |
